sections.body: The American Hotel & Lodging Association publishes this page as its homepage. It is a landing page, not a report, standard, or technical document. It presents AHLA as a national hotel industry association and points to advocacy, membership, events, discounts, updates, a political action committee, a state facts dashboard, an allied attorney directory, and resources. sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page states that AHLA champions the hotel industry through advocacy, resources, and initiatives that strengthen hospitality businesses and workforce nationwide. It says hotels and the lodging industry create career possibilities and economically strengthen communities across the country. It invites readers to contact elected officials and describes HotelPAC as AHLA's voluntary, bi-partisan political action committee formed to help elect federal candidates who support the lodging industry. It promotes AHLA connections, events, discounts, breaking updates, and advocacy. It points to a State Facts dashboard on state-by-state economic impact and an Allied Attorney Directory. It notes that U.S. Travel Association, Airlines for America, and AHLA urge Congress to resolve funding differences and protect America's travel system. A Vanteo item says developing an effective and compliant global talent strategy is critical for hoteliers and mentions J-1, H-2B, and EB-3 visa programs. AHLA says it champions legislation supporting hoteliers, operators, and employees by engaging federal, state, and local policymakers. It lists initiatives in sustainability, workforce development, and human trafficking prevention. It offers resources, policy talking points, and industry best practices. It describes a diverse membership of brand companies, owners, management companies, independents, suppliers, and state lodging and aligned hospitality associations, spanning every segment of the hospitality ecosystem, with unified advocacy on Capitol Hill and local engagement resources.
